open.speaker: regulars
lines: Coffee's on me, fellas. What's the real story?
Real story is high school kids. They go out to the igloos with flashlights and those red bicycle reflectors.
Scare their girlfriends, scare the papers. Same as every year.

passives.line: 'Same as every year.' He answered when it started before you asked. Men who have been asked before keep the answer ready.
Three men, three cups, and a fourth cup turned upside down on its saucer. Somebody belongs in that seat.

options.text: Every year? Those kids must be pushing thirty by now.
We ran the Kessler garage story in Columbus last month. Just confirming.
Those reflectors on the truck out front. Same kind?

years.speaker: regulars
lines: Different kids. Same reflectors. Harmon's sells 'em ten cents a pair and has since Eisenhower.
Hank here saw it in '66. Go on, Hank. Tell 'em what you saw.
That pause was three seconds long. I counted.

passives.line: Hank did not see a crane. Hank saw the inside of this booth for twenty-eight years with men who say he saw a crane.

fourth.speaker: regulars
lines: Lyle. Lyle Beckett. He's on the plaque down by the river, second column.
He had the cup turned up the morning of December 15th, 1967. We turned it down the 16th and nobody's touched it.
Second column. My uncle's in the third.

passives.line: A cup turned down for the dead. Your grandmother did the same with a chair. You do not ask them to move it; you ask them nothing for a minute.

kessler_bluff.speaker: regulars
lines: Columbus. Huh. Well, if it's in Columbus already there's no harm.
Bobby Kessler and his cousin. Garage on Sixth Street. The board's hanging on the wall like a deer head.
Sixth Street. I'd have got there without the lie, but I'll take it.

passives.line: Columbus was a good choice. Far enough that nobody here reads it, close enough that they believe it exists.

bluff_fail.speaker: regulars
lines: Columbus. Hank, you hear that? Columbus has got our garage story.
Son, nobody in Columbus has ever printed the word 'Kessler'. You want to lie, lie about something we can't check from this booth.

passives.line: Shake it off. You got caught by three men with a combined age of two hundred. Sit up, you are not leaving this booth yet.

truck.speaker: regulars
lines: Hell, every kid in the county's got 'em. Every truck too. Doesn't make a monster.
Monster's in the headlights. Hold one up at head height and it's whatever you came out there to see.
Hold one up at head height in February for an hour. See how long you last.

truck_fail.speaker: regulars
lines: Them's off my boat trailer, and you're not a boat man, so don't.
You want reflectors, there's a kid on the corner by the courthouse with a pocketful. Ask him where he's taking 'em.

passives.line: Boat trailer reflectors are oblong. Bicycle ones are round. You did not look before you spoke.

quiet.speaker: regulars
lines: ...Anyway, Hank's grandson's on the team this year. Guard.
He don't go out to the igloos. Says the other boys stopped going too. Says something's been out there since Thursday that ain't reflectors.
Kids. You know how they get.

passives.line: They forgot you were there. That is the only way this booth ever says anything true.

hub.speaker: regulars
lines: You still here? Sit, then. Booth's got room.
